Move Over 'James Bondisson' and GTA VI Because Lamborghini Rocked LA With the Temerario Spyder
14 photos
Photo: Lamborghini
This has been a very interesting week, and the ongoing 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show is the culmination of things for automotive fans – the ones that don’t feel sad or enraged about Robert Pattinson being cast by Amazon MGM Studios as the next James Bond and the ones that aren’t too tired after playing non-stop GTA VI since it launched, that is.
I kind of fell out of bed on Monday morning when I heard that none of the final-five actors that were in the books to play the next James Bond actually got the part, and Amazon MGM Studios went with the ‘safe’ casting of Twilight-saga star Robert Pattinson. There’s a lot to talk about the Hollywood star, who has worked hard to get rid of the shiny vampire banter over his formative years.
Some will like this idea; others will not. I have mixed feelings – I would have loved to see a relatively unknown actor take over the mantle and make James Bond their own just like Daniel Craig, Pierce Brosnan, or the late and beloved Sean Connery did in their times. I think that it’s a Disney move to play it safe with someone who already has a ton of work behind their back.
There’s also the situation with The Batman – this guy may be a cool and modern Hollywood star, but he’s not immortal (pun intended) and doesn’t have time to commit to a couple of massive franchises at the same time. However, there is one major glimmer of hope – the next 007 installment is being directed by Denis Villeneuve, which I think is one of those directors like Christopher Nolan who can live up to the standards of blockbusters imposed by Steven Spielberg and James Cameron.
Photo: Amazon MGM Also, we can already make fun of the casting – the viral portmanteau nickname for Robert Pattinson and his new Amazon MGM role is “James Bondisson,” created in line with Barbenheimer or the upcoming Dunesday. Now, let’s talk about the big elephant in the PlayStation and Xbox realm – Grand Theft Auto VI . By the way, I have a confession to make.
Although I loved playing games when I was in my prime – those years when girls and cars were the only things that mattered (along with planes, at least for me) – the GTA franchise never spoke to my heart, as I would rather play Call of Duty or Diablo or even NFS instead. But my adolescent kid has taken a liking to GTA V, so of course I’m in touch with the 13-year wait for the sixth installment.
The new game came out this week precisely when 007 is also new, and Anthropic has also gone for IPO greatness on top of everything – just to also touch on the hot subject of AI and avoid any Nvidia and its ousted CEO discussions. So, for me, GTA VI hasn’t been a major interest – though I did stay in touch, especially poking fun with my boy (who is patiently waiting for the game as a gift sometime down the line) about folks taking a week off from work and even signing agreements with their spouses and kids to make sure they’re not disturbed.
Photo: Rockstar Games One thing I did keep a closer eye on was the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show , which used to be a major draw for automakers because it’s the final hurrah of the automotive season ahead of the Christmas holidays. Unfortunately, either because of a confluence of factors or due to the James Bondisson, Anthropic IPO, and especially the GTA VI off time of employees, this year’s Automobility LA and the LA Auto Show itself have been rather bland and uninteresting.
That’s not to say there weren’t any cool premieres, like the Rivian R2, the eighth generation of the Hyundai Elantra, the 2027 Chrysler Pacifica Copperline, and a bunch of other minor novelties from the likes of Acura and Honda all the way up to Volkswagen. In fact, I think the Elantra deserves a ton of appreciation because Hyundai continues to cater to the affordable compact sedan space.
Photo: Lamborghini However, the coolest automobile this week is the new Lamborghini Temerario Spyder launched on the eve of the 2026 LA Auto Show both in Sant’Agata Bolognese and Los Angeles. Well, if you asked me about the coupe before this release, I would have said the Huracan successor is a nice technical tour de force but also a little bland, especially when seen from the front because the rear can’t make any mistakes when you’re mid-engined and packing 907 hp.
But somehow, without changing the front, which remains boring, the rear is a festival of coolness thanks to that crazy vertical-stowing hardtop roof that not only makes the Temerario look like a real Spyder, as if there’s no roof whatsoever, but also enhances handling because of a lower center of gravity when the car is roofless. Now I really hope the Revuelto Roadster goes down the same route… View this post on Instagram A post shared by James Bond 007 (@007) View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rockstar Games (@rockstargames)
